content.value: Inclusive interfaces are stronger for everyone. Prioritize semantic HTML, keyboard focus, clear focus states, proper labels, and sufficient color contrast. Accessibility is part of quality, not an optional add-on at the end.

concepts.name: Semantic HTML
concepts.description: HTML that uses elements according to their meaning and role rather than only for visual layout.

concepts.name: Keyboard navigation
concepts.description: The ability to use an interface through keyboard controls instead of a mouse or touch input.

concepts.name: Focus state
concepts.description: The visual or programmatic indication of which interactive element is currently selected for keyboard input.

concepts.name: Color contrast
concepts.description: The difference in brightness and color between text and background that affects readability.

concepts.name: ARIA
concepts.description: Attributes that provide accessibility semantics when native HTML cannot express the needed role or state.

concepts.name: Accessible name
concepts.description: The text label assistive technologies use to identify an interactive element.
